JAYESH SINGH · EXPERIMENT AUDIT

LLM sampling settings & token efficiency

143 included runs · 180,837 total tokens · temperature 0.7 excluded

JAYESH SINGH | PORTFOLIO CASE STUDY | 18 NOVEMBER 2026

Decoding settings and token efficiency

143 analyzed runs · 3 logged models · 11 exact prompt versions · 40 configurations. An observational audit of sampling settings, API-reported token usage and mechanically checkable outputs. Source: llm_outputs.txt, recorded 17 November 2026.

Scope: 153 records parsed; all 10 runs at temperature 0.7 excluded from every reported statistic and chart. The earlier top-p 0.7 exclusion also applies; no such entries exist. Included usage: 28,503 input + 152,334 output = 180,837 total tokens.

Logged modelRunsInput sumOutput sumTotal sumMean outputMedian outputMean totalMedian total
GPT-4o-mini6910,9426,31317,25591.4948.00250.07314.00
Luna6817,102144,861161,9632,130.311,915.002,381.812,180.00
Mistral Nemo64591,1601,619193.33256.00269.83274.00

These pooled model figures describe the recorded workload. They are not a fair model ranking: the models received different tasks, prompt revisions, settings and caps.

What the data supports

1. Stronger result, larger token footprint on the matched grid task. Luna produced the correct normalized letter sequence in 5/5 runs versus GPT-4o-mini in 0/10. Mean total tokens were 2,849.40 versus 308.80: 9.23x as many. This is a single-puzzle, small-sample result.

2. Mean and median select different Luna settings. On the grid with cap 10,000, T=1, p=0 had the lowest observed mean output (2,045.20); T=2, p=0 had the lowest median (1,856.00). Both returned 5/5 correct sequences.

3. Failure accounting matters. Two cap-hitting Luna calls returned empty text and consumed 3,530 total tokens. Those calls and every high-token outlier remain included. No dollar cost or latency is inferred.

METHODS AND AUDIT

Measurement, scoring and verification

CheckResult
Full-record parsingTwo independent parsers agree on all 153 records, including prompts and responses.
Raw structure7,068 lines; 223,858 bytes; every header and record separator reconciled.
Token accountingInput + output = total for 153/153 records; no negative token counts.
ExclusionTemperature 0.7: original run IDs 71, 72, 73, 74, 75, 93, 94, 95, 96, 97. No top-p 0.7 entries.
Summary recomputationAll 40 setting groups recomputed with Python statistics and exact rational means/quantiles, independently of pandas.
Chart verification558 raw plotted marks and 113 summary values reconciled; all 143 runs plotted for each token field.
Export verificationAll 153 audit rows round-tripped through CSV with unchanged token counts, prompts and responses.

Grouping: exact system prompt + user prompt, model label, temperature, top-p and max-token cap. Prompt IDs are assigned in source order. Prompt whitespace is preserved after normalizing CRLF to LF. Runs are not deduplicated merely because answers repeat.

Statistics: arithmetic mean; ordinary sample median; sample SD (n - 1 denominator; undefined at n=1); Q1, Q3 and P90 by linear interpolation; IQR = Q3 - Q1; CV = 100 x SD / mean. Tables display two decimals; calculations use unrounded values. Group input tokens are constant, so mean input = median input = the displayed input value. Overall medians are computed directly from rows, never by adding or averaging subgroup medians.

Scoring: sorting uses the exact ordered integer list. Letter puzzles compare the entire response after lowercasing and removing nonletters with a programmatically derived reference. Both references are independently derived twice. This measures letter-sequence correctness, not strict formatting. A separate spacing-only check preserves case and punctuation. Factual QA and car prose are not scored for factual correctness.

Measurement limits: the log records input/output/total tokens, not a visible-text tokenization, bill, latency, finish reason, reasoning-token breakdown, seed, provider request ID or effective server-side parameter handling. Model names and settings are reported exactly as logged. The retrieved prior chat provides experiment context but is not evidence that a particular request option was applied to these calls. No inferential or causal claim is made.

All 18 retained runs produced the correct normalized sequence. The mean rose from 513.60 at T=0 to 655.20 at T=2 (27.57% higher), but peaked at T=1.5, so the observed relationship is not monotonic. Mean input and median input are 214 in every group.

Visible answers were only six words, with two raw-text variants differing by the final period, while reported output usage ranged from 414 to 946 tokens. This discrepancy cannot be decomposed into reasoning or other token categories from this log. There is no observed accuracy benefit from the higher-token settings on this one item.

Correct = normalized letter-sequence success. Total tokens per success = all total tokens in the setting, including failures, divided by its successful runs. It is an observed ratio, not an estimate of expected retry cost. P90 is unstable with only five or six repeats; raw values and ranges are supplied alongside it.

Change = 100 x (p=0 value / p=1 value - 1); negative means fewer tokens at p=0. The observed mean decreases at three temperatures and increases at T=1.5. Medians decrease at all four. These are descriptive contrasts from small, uneven, non-randomized groups; they do not prove how the backend implemented top-p or establish a universally best setting.

Luna used 60.38x the mean output tokens and 9.23x the mean total tokens while producing 5/5 correct sequences versus 0/10. GPT-4o-mini's observed tokens-per-success value is undefined, because it had no successes. Low token usage alone does not show useful task efficiency.

These settings match on the logged fields, but samples were taken sequentially and no seed, backend fingerprint or reasoning configuration is recorded. This supports a result on this puzzle and endpoint, not a general capability ranking or a dollar-cost comparison.

These rows hold Luna, P11, T=0 and p=1 fixed. The one call at each lower cap returned no visible text, with output usage exactly equal to the cap. They consumed 1,265 + 2,265 = 3,530 total tokens. The 10,000-cap group returned 6/6 correct sequences. Finish reasons are absent, so truncation is plausible but not confirmed, and two single runs cannot establish a reliable minimum budget.

The normalized letter-sequence grade tolerates case and punctuation. Under a literal spacing-only transformation (remove whitespace, preserve every other character), P10 passes 0/18 and Luna P11 passes 19/50. This stricter score is kept separate so answer correctness is not confused with complete instruction compliance.

CLAIMS THAT MATCH THE EXPERIMENT

Portfolio conclusions and resume wording

Use this resume bullet

Built a reproducible LLM evaluation workflow across 143 API runs, 3 models and 40 prompt/parameter configurations; reconciled 180,837 tokens with two independent parsers, verified every plotted value, and measured token distributions, deterministic answer correctness and failure-inclusive token efficiency.

Use this results paragraph in the project README

After excluding ten temperature-0.7 runs, I analyzed 143 calls across 11 exact prompt versions. On the shared 64-letter puzzle at temperature 0, top-p 0 and a 10,000-token limit, Luna returned the correct normalized letter sequence in 5/5 attempts versus GPT-4o-mini in 0/10, with mean total usage of 2,849.40 versus 308.80 tokens. I kept blank responses and outliers in the accounting and separated comparisons by prompt and token cap. Results are descriptive repeated-run observations, not a general model benchmark.

Conclusions and limits

Supported: setting-dependent token variability in the recorded Luna calls; stable mini output length on the simpler tasks; a quality-versus-token tradeoff on the matched grid puzzle; and a visible difference between token-cap exhaustion, correct output and strict character compliance.

Not established: a universal optimal temperature or top-p; significant population-level differences; general model accuracy; dollar savings; latency; effective backend sampler behavior; or an explanation of the unexposed output-token usage. The samples are small, uneven, sequential and adaptively collected, with just one item per task/prompt version.

A focused follow-up experiment

Freeze prompts and references before running. Test the same models and complete setting grid on multiple newly generated, programmatically validated puzzles. Randomize call order; use equal repeated-call counts; log the exact request, response model ID, token-detail fields, finish reason, latency and price basis. Predeclare normalized correctness and strict formatting as separate endpoints. Report per-item results before aggregating.

Reproduction and provenance

Run python analyze_llm_runs.py llm_outputs.txt --out results with numpy, pandas and matplotlib. The script reproduces the audited tables, six charts and validation manifest without API calls. The companion HTML contains all run values, original prompts/responses and downloadable supporting files.

Source SHA-256: 4446216c00269791ea852c3c0889aa0dae43c0ca36bdd8fad0e4eccdfacd126d. The original source log is unchanged. Verification means zero discrepancies detected by the documented checks; it is not an absolute guarantee about source-provider billing or hidden runtime behavior.
